enunciado: “I ___ these old photos when I was tidying the closet.” (found by chance)
explicacion:
✔ *I came across these old photos when I was tidying the closet.*

Come across = find or meet unexpectedly.

✔ *Our car broke down in the snowstorm.*

Break down = stop working (machines). It also means start crying (people).

✔ *This sad music is bringing me down.*

Bring someone down = make someone sad.

enunciado: “My father always ___ sports at dinner.” (starts talking about)
explicacion:
✔ *My father always brings up sports at dinner.*

Bring something up = introduce a topic.

enunciado: “You can always ___ Michael in a crisis.”
explicacion:
✔ *You can always count on Michael in a crisis.*

Count on = rely on, trust.

enunciado: “It's a fancy restaurant, so we have to ___.”
explicacion:
✔ *It's a fancy restaurant, so we have to dress up.*

Dress up = wear elegant clothes.

enunciado: “I have to ___ my sister ___ at work.” (take her there by car)
explicacion:
✔ *I have to drop my sister off at work.*

Drop someone off = leave them somewhere, usually by car. The pronoun goes in the middle: drop her off.

enunciado: “We ___ renting a movie instead of going out.” (not planned)
explicacion:
✔ *We ended up renting a movie instead of going out.*

End up = finally be in a situation you didn't plan.

enunciado: “Brian ___ Judy ___ to dinner.” (invited her on a date)
explicacion:
✔ *Brian asked Judy out to dinner.*

Ask someone out = invite someone on a date.

enunciado: “Tom invited Sue to dinner, but she ___ him ___.” (refused)
explicacion:
✔ *Tom invited Sue to dinner, but she turned him down.*

Turn down = refuse an invitation or offer.

enunciado: “She fainted, but ___ about five minutes later.”
explicacion:
✔ *She fainted, but came to about five minutes later.*

Come to = regain consciousness.

enunciado: “Would you like to ___ next Thursday?” (visit my house)
explicacion:
✔ *Would you like to come over next Thursday?*

Come over = visit someone's home. Pass by = go past a place.

enunciado: “Maria has never ___ with the crowd.” (felt she belonged)
explicacion:
✔ *Maria has never fitted in with the crowd.*

Fit in = belong to a group. Put on = wear; get in = arrive home.

enunciado: What makes a phrasal verb different from a verb + preposition?
opciones: It is only used in writing
explicacion: In verb + preposition (wait for) the meaning stays the same as the verb. In a phrasal verb (break down) the particle creates a new meaning.
